extracted.intended_audience: USPTO examiners and reexamination unit staff; patent practitioners and third-party requesters seeking guidance on inter partes reexamination procedure
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive standards from the MPEP governing handling, assignment, timing, decision criteria, and processing of inter partes reexamination requests and proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Event reporting obligations (PALM/IFW)
rubrics_metrics.description: The CRU support staff is responsible for reporting reexamination-related events using the reexamination icon and window initiated in the PALM EXPO program. Events to be reported are enumerated (see guidance). All events will be permanently recorded and displayed in the 'Contents' portion of PALM; status representative of these events will also be displayed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Events to be reported include: (1) Determination Mailed - Denial of request for reexamination; (2) Determination Mailed - Grant of request for reexamination; (3) Petition for reconsideration of determination received; (4) Decision on petition mailed - Denied; (5) Decision on petition mailed - Granted; (6) Mailing of all examiner actions; (7) Patent owner responses to Office Actions; (8) Third party requester comments after a patent owner response. Various weekly 'tickler' reports can be generated for each TC from these event reports to assure reexaminations are processed with 'special dispatch.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner assignment of reexamination proceeding (general rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reexamination requests will normally be assigned to the Central Reexamination Unit (CRU) art unit which examines the relevant technology. The CRU Supervisory Patent Examiner (SPE) assigns the reexamination request to a primary examiner who is most familiar with the claimed subject matter and who is different from the examiner(s) who examined the original patent application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A primary examiner assigned should not be the same examiner who examined the patent application, prepared/signed an action, or participated as a conferee in appeal/panel conferences in the earlier examination; in rare situations where proceeding remains in a TC, an assistant examiner may be assigned but a primary examiner must sign and take responsibility for all actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner assignment exceptions and approval requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Exceptions to assigning a different examiner include cases where the original examiner is the only one with adequate knowledge of the relevant technology to examine the case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the original examiner must be assigned, the assignment must be approved by the CRU Director and that approval must be stated in the decision on the request for reexamination (and noted by the examiner).

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment where earlier reexamination is ongoing
rubrics_metrics.description: If an earlier reexamination is still ongoing, the same examiner who handled the earlier (still ongoing) reexamination may be assigned to a newly filed reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an explicitly permitted exception to the general assignment-exclusion rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copending reissue and reexamination assignment and merger handling
rubrics_metrics.description: When a reissue application is pending and a reexamination request is filed for the same patent, or vice versa, special assignment and merger rules apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If reexamination is granted and the reissue and reexamination are merged, the merged proceeding will be handled by a TC examiner other than the examiner who examined the original patent application; reissue application may be reassigned accordingly. If reexamination has not yet been ordered, a TC Quality Assurance Specialist ensures the reissue application is not assigned/acted on until the decision on reexamination; OPLA is notified for merger consideration and hand-delivery of paper files where applicable. If proceedings are not merged, assignment guidance will be provided in the decision depending on facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for challenging inadvertent assignment to original examiner
rubrics_metrics.description: If a reexamination is inadvertently assigned to an original examiner without required Director approval indicated in the decision, the patent owner or third-party requester who objects must promptly file a paper alerting the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any request challenging assignment must be made within two months of the first Office action or other Office communication indicating the examiner assignment, or reassignment will not be considered. Reassignment will be addressed case-by-case. Assignment to the original examiner, by itself, is not grounds for vacating Office decisions or restarting the reexamination. In limited situations where a paper lacks right of entry (e.g., before first action on merits), the Office may waive rules to enter and consider the paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transfer procedure between art units
rubrics_metrics.description: If the CRU SPE believes the reexamination should be assigned to another art unit, the transferring SPE must obtain consent of the receiving CRU SPE; transfers must be conducted with special dispatch per 35 U.S.C. 314(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The transferring SPE should expeditiously request transfer to the 'new' art unit, hand-carry paper patent files where applicable to the receiving SPE, and any conflicts unresolved by the SPEs are resolved by the CRU Director.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time reporting for reexamination activities
rubrics_metrics.description: All USPTO personnel must report all time expended on reexamination activities on their individual Time and Attendance Reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This includes supervision, copying, typing, docketing and other ancillary activities because reexamination fees are based on full cost recovery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory deadline for decision on request (3-month rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director (and under delegation the examiner) must determine whether a substantial new question of patentability is raised not later than three months after the filing of the request for inter partes reexamination (35 U.S.C. 312; 37 CFR 1.923).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner's determination is based on the claims in effect at the time of the determination, becomes part of the official file, and is mailed to the patent owner and third-party requester. If the 3-month period ends on a weekend or federal holiday in D.C., mailing must be by the preceding business day.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner must perform and record litigation review (STIC search)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to making a determination on the request, the examiner must request a litigation search by the Scientific and Technical Information Center (STIC) to check if the patent has been or is involved in litigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A copy of the STIC search is scanned into the IFW reexamination file history; the 'Litigation Review' box on the IFW file jacket form is completed to indicate review and results. If litigation is or was involved and a paper referring to the court proceeding has been filed, reference to the paper by number should be placed in the Litigation Review box. If litigation exists, the case must be promptly brought to the attention of the Reexamination Legal Advisor assigned to the case for review to ensure conformance with litigation policy and guidelines (see MPEP § 2686.04).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims to be considered in determination (claims-in-effect rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner's determination is based on the patent claims in effect at the time of the determination and will not consider amendments filed in a copending reexamination or reissue where a reexamination certificate or reissue patent has not yet issued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The decision on the request should discuss all patent claims requested for reexamination, but should limit discussion to whether a substantial new question of patentability has been raised. The examiner SHOULD NOT reject claims in the order for reexamination; any rejection is made in the first Office action that normally accompanies the order for reexamination (see MPEP § 2660). Only one claim needs a substantial new question of patentability to order reexamination. If a request fails to apply the art to certain claims as required, those claims generally will not be reexamined; the Office may at its discretion reexamine non-requested claims or initiate reexamination on its own.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requester content requirement: pertinency and manner of applying cited art
rubrics_metrics.description: A requester must 'set forth the pertinency and manner of applying cited prior art to every claim for which reexamination is requested' (35 U.S.C. 311(b)(2); 37 CFR 1.915(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the requester fails to apply the art to certain claims as required, the requester is not statutorily entitled to reexamination of such claims. A failure to set forth pertinency and manner as required by 37 CFR 1.915(b) may result in no filing date being awarded to the request. See MPEP §§ 2617 and 2627 for filing date consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and standard for 'substantial new question of patentability' (SNQ)
rubrics_metrics.description: A prior art patent or printed publication raises a substantial new question of patentability where there is a substantial likelihood that a reasonable examiner would consider the prior art important in deciding the patentability of at least one claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For SNQ to be present: (A) the prior art teaches something a reasonable examiner would consider important for at least one claim; and (B) the same question of patentability has not been decided by the Office in a previous examination or pending reexamination or by a final federal court holding on the claim. It is not necessary to establish a prima facie case of unpatentability to show an SNQ (i.e., SNQ can exist even if the examiner would not necessarily reject the claim on the merits). Newly provided prior art that is merely cumulative to art already fully considered may not raise an SNQ.

rubrics_metrics.name: Second or subsequent request standard (different SNQ requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a second or subsequent request is filed while a first reexamination is pending, the presence of an SNQ depends on the art cited by the subsequent request and whether that art raises a substantial new question different from that in the pending reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the subsequent request includes the same art that raised the SNQ in the earlier pending reexamination, the subsequent request should be denied. If it raises a different SNQ as to some claims but not others, the request may be granted in part. The subsequent requester must independently provide an SNQ different from that raised in the pending reexamination for the claims in effect at the time of determination. Once a different SNQ is established, the subsequent request may also provide information directed to proposed new or amended claims in the pending reexamination to permit examination of the entire patent package. If the patent owner can show the later request was filed for harassment, the owner may petition under 37 CFR 1.182 to suspend the second proceeding; if granted, prosecution of the later request may be suspended until conclusion of the first reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on subsequent inter partes requests by same requester (37 CFR 1.907(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Once an order for inter partes reexamination has been issued, neither the third party requester of that inter partes reexamination, nor its privies, may file a subsequent request for inter partes reexamination of the same patent until an inter partes reexamination certificate has been issued, unless expressly authorized by the Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A petition for such authorization is extraordinary relief and will not normally be granted where conventional avenues exist to accomplish the same purpose. This prohibition tracks 35 U.S.C. 317(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing timeline and internal action deadlines (CRU/examiner/RLA flow)
rubrics_metrics.description: Internal processing timelines are prescribed to meet the 3-month statutory decision requirement and ensure special dispatch.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typically CRU forwards the case to the examiner within two weeks of filing. The examiner has one week from receipt to prepare for an initial consultation conference with the Reexamination Legal Advisor (RLA). After consultation the examiner has two weeks to prepare the decision on the request and an Office action (if reexamination is granted) and forward to the CRU SPE. At the latest, the decision and action must be hand-carried to the RLA within nine weeks from the filing date of the request (unless authorized otherwise by the CRU Director or RLA). The first Office action ordinarily accompanies the order for reexamination, but if issuing the first action would delay the order past a critical deadline, the order will be mailed and the first action will follow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refunds and petitions relating to refusal to order reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: If inter partes reexamination is not ordered, a partial refund of the requester fee may be made under 37 CFR 1.925 and § 1.26(c). The third-party requester may seek review of a refusal to order reexamination by petition to the Director under 37 CFR 1.181 within one month of the mailing date of the examiner's determination (37 CFR 1.927).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any such petition must comply with § 1.181(b). If no petition is timely filed or the petition affirms that no SNQ was raised, the determination is final and nonappealable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requests filed after reissue or where reissue issues after request
rubrics_metrics.description: If a reexamination request is filed on a patent after a reissue patent for that patent has already issued, the reexamination will be denied because the original patent has been surrendered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To reexamine a reissued patent, a new request must be filed based on the specification and claims of the reissue patent. If the reissue patent issues after filing of a request, special handling and merger rules apply (see MPEP § 2686.03).
